findings.title: Restarted flusher gets a new SpansBuffer, losing the old buffer's state
findings.body: Every restart of a process (`_create_process_for_shards`) builds a fresh `SpansBuffer(shards)` and overwrites `self.buffers[process_index]`. Any per-buffer state held by the old one (for example `any_shard_at_limit` and the counters read by `record_stored_segments`) is lost. A related problem is that the old thread or process is not stopped when the cause is `hang` and the process is a thread: the `kill` is skipped for non-`multiprocessing.Process` objects. Two flushers can then run on the same shards at once and produce duplicate segments.

findings.title: isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) never matches a SpawnProcess
findings.body: Processes are created from the spawn context, so they are `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess` instances. `SpawnProcess` subclasses `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`, not `multiprocessing.Process`, which is a different class (`multiprocessing.context.Process`). The isinstance check in `join` and in `_ensure_processes_alive` is therefore always False. Hung flusher processes are never killed on restart, and `terminate()` is never called on shutdown. Leaked processes then run alongside their replacements.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag name: `shards` vs `shard`
findings.body: `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is tagged `shards`, while the other new metrics use `shard`. Dashboards that group by one tag name will miss the other metric's data.

findings.title: join() timeout handling breaks early and skips terminating the remaining processes
findings.body: When the deadline passes, the loop `break`s and never calls `terminate()` on the remaining processes. They are left running (daemon only). `deadline` is also None when `timeout` is 0, which makes `join` wait indefinitely.

findings.title: Test uses a real time.sleep and does not verify multi-process flushing
findings.body: `time.sleep` is monkeypatched to a no-op at the top of the test, so the added `time.sleep(0.1)` does nothing and the wait is racy. `test_flusher_processes_limit` only checks the shard-to-process mapping. Nothing tests the restart path or backpressure across several processes.
